turns.content: Hey! So I spent basically all Saturday chasing this crazy OD600 scatter — like 0.18 to 0.42 across identical controls 🔬😩. Finally pinned it down to microcentrifuge tubes warming on the bench before acid precipitation. Anyway, I pulled up the method sheet for our succinate dehydrogenase assay — the 10% TCA precipitation step in 50 mM phosphate buffer pH 7.4, then spinning at 4°C. The phrasing about pre-cooling the centrifuge is kinda ambiguous though ❓. My read is you have to keep tubes on crushed ice before the spin to stop residual substrate turnover — does that match the protocol?
I'll check the method sheet you pulled up so I can match the TCA/spin wording instead of guessing. 🔍

Oh yeah that's the part that was driving me crazy — "pre-cool the rotor" but nothing about the tubes themselves ❓ So you're saying the spin temp matters but the quench timing isn't explicitly covered? That's basically what I figured from the scatter data, but it'd be great to have a second pair of eyes confirm I'm not over-interpreting
I’ll look at the method sheet itself so we can check the TCA / rotor wording against what you actually saw, not just the scatter story. 🔍

Wait so if the rotor pre-cool is covered but tube temp isn't explicitly spelled out... that's pretty much what I ran into Saturday 😅. Does the method sheet actually say anything about keeping tubes on ice, or is that just implied by "maintain 4°C throughout"?
I’ll pull the method sheet and check the TCA / 4°C wording directly so we can see what’s written vs. what’s implied. 🔍

Alright yeah I think I want to add a note to the lab binder about this — Priya's rotating in next month and I'd rather she not burn a Saturday like I did 😅. Should I just write "keep tubes on ice until spin" or is there a more general note about bench warming that'd help for other assays too?
I’ll grab any lab-protocol notes we already have so the binder wording matches your assay, not a generic ice-bucket sermon. 🧊

Alright, I'll try to get to the binder note this weekend, but honestly just feeling pretty good about having cracked the scatter thing — was that whole Saturday, so you know, nice to have it sorted 😅. Does that fix seem like it'd apply to the acid precipitation steps in the older protocols too, or is that just me overgeneralizing?
I’ll look through the method sheet and any older protocols you’ve got so we can see whether the ice/bench-warming issue is written in, implied, or just your Saturday-lab wisdom. 🧊
